C08-M06-L04-F1.title: The MISP data model
C08-M06-L04-F1.caption: An event contains attributes and template-based objects, is labelled with taxonomy tags and galaxy clusters, and receives sightings from consumers against its attributes.
C08-M06-L04-F1.alt: Graph. Event (info, date, threat level, analysis, distribution) contains Attribute (category, type, value, to_ids) and contains Object (template: file, url, domain-ip). Object groups Attribute and has an Object reference (relationship type). Event and Attribute are each tagged with Tag (taxonomy), for example tlp:amber and Admiralty scale. Event relates to Galaxy cluster (ATT&CK technique, threat actor). Sighting (seen, false positive, expired) points to Attribute, labelled about.

nodes.label: Event
nodes.sub: info, date, threat level, analysis, distribution

C08-M06-L04-F1.note: Automation reads the model: values, flags, tags and distribution, never free-text titles.

C08-M06-L04-F2.title: Correlation: a meaningful link and over-correlation control
C08-M06-L04-F2.caption: Two events sharing a specific value are linked by exact-match correlation, while a common value is caught by a warninglist and kept out of correlation.
C08-M06-L04-F2.alt: Graph with two independent groups. First group: Event A: Banyan intrusion (domain cdn-telemetry-sync.example) and Event B: ISAC-A loader report (same domain) both lead to Correlation: exact value match, which leads to Related events linked (independent sources corroborate). Second group: Common value in many events (shared CDN or resolver address) leads to Warninglist match (known false-positive list), which leads to Exclude or disable correlation (avoid over-correlation).
C08-M06-L04-F2.note: A correlation is a lead to investigate, not a conclusion about who is behind it.
